Backend-specific dependency edits and tests remain d-6..d-9 owned.
- 3. Update sc-config/sc-transport/sc-runtime READMEs alongside changed API/dependency behavior; preserve documented test-util helper and synchronous sc-config scope — REQ-RUN-0702; NFR-CFG-0002; NFR-RT-0001.

Preserve the unpublished compile-fail fixture crates/sc-runtime/tests/fixtures/utoipa5-router/Cargo.toml with incompatible utoipa-axum ^0.2.0; it is test input, not a published SDK or template dependency. design
CompatibleOpen dependencyregistry policyfloors (ANC-016/019):and tested recommendations (ANC-037/038):
- Published crate and template requirements permit every newer Cargo
- SemVer-compatible dependency release under their supported API, native-link,
- and Rust-toolchain contract. Consumers can use `cargo update` without another
- sc-runtime release (ANC-016). Normal requirements such as `rmcp = "3.9.0"`
- already allow compatible 3.x updates; blanket support for future breaking
- versions is not promised. Preserve existing dependency features.
+ Every registry dependency requirement in published crates and templates uses >= a tested floor with no upper bound, including SDK dependencies. Convert bare-version and caret requirements as well as exact/tilde pins. Consumers may pin any versions in their own manifests or lockfiles. The release recommends its tested combination instead of restricting consumer choices (owner m6 extension; ANC-037). Preserve existing dependency features.
Rusqlite qualification and its one manifest owner are d-6; this sprint does not repeat that work.
- Each additional upper bound tighter than the normal compatible range has a
- TOML comment immediately beside the requirement naming the concrete API,
- native-link, or toolchain break that requires that specific bound (ANC-019).
- The actual optional Monty requirements retain their optional status:
-
- ```toml
- # Monty 1.6 requires Rust 1.98; supported Monty CI uses Rust 1.96.1.
- monty = { version = ">=1.4.0, <1.6", optional = true }
- # monty-types 1.6 requires Rust 1.98; supported Monty CI uses Rust 1.96.1.
- monty-types = { version = ">=1.4.0, <1.6", optional = true }
- ```
-
- Exact/tilde restrictions need the same demonstrated incompatibility rationale.
- Intentional negative compatibility fixtures retain their incompatible test
- identity with a manifest comment; they do not constrain production consumers.
+ Monty and monty-types remain optional and use >=1.4.0. The normal suite tests the selected versions on the documented toolchain. Intentional non-shipped negative fixtures retain their incompatible identity; they do not constrain consumers.
- The root Cargo.toml currently declares only sc-observability-types as a workspace dependency; rmcp and other actual third-party declarations are in crate manifests. This sprint owns explicit sc-config/sc-transport/sc-runtime manifests and enumerated command/runtime compatibility source, no crates/** wildcard. d-5 owns root Cargo.toml registration; d-12 owns canonical Cargo.lock/version conversion, shared template manifests and contract versions. The contract owner applies only the agreed range edits in those shared files; d-3 owns runnable endpoint qualification, not their concurrent mutation. Local endpoint tests may use disposable locks; d-12 regenerates/commits the final canonical lock after source owners close. No hard dependency on d-5 is inferred from release baseline.
- sc-command Cargo.toml (d-5) and lib.rs/README/storage.rs/tests/storage_combinators.rs (d-10) are explicit exclusions from this owner's enumerated source/test paths. Current API adaptation files are enumerated, not hidden behind wildcard ownership. Existing features/schema negative fixtures remain meaningful; preserve utoipa5 rejection fixtures and narrow their incompatible identities only with existing adjacent reasons. Source adaptations do not add ATM/sc-compose production dependencies.
Closure note: integration applies to this complete independent feature, even in the first wave; its actual API/toolchain interactions and executable acceptance close here, not an unimplemented contract.

## Proposed signaturescontracts — prototypeprototype, andthen freezeowner at contract closureratification
ThesePhase-d defineimplements realname/mode productiontransaction APIs,properties notand test-directoryfinite replicas.engine Proposedretry/deadline exactdefaults. handle/mapping design is theThe contract sprint'spermits prototypeadding risk,a not an already user-decided implementation. Only name and mode are transaction properties;transaction-specific retry policy remainslater; enginethat implementationoption detail.is not implemented in phase-d. TransactionSpec uses constructors/builders and a non-exhaustive public shape rather than requiring consumer struct literals. Real exported interfaces live in sc-storage; no test-directory signature copies.
```rust
// sc-storage; std-only, no sc-*, SQLx, rusqlite, ATM or sc-compose deps.
use std::{future::Future,pin::Pin};
pub enum TransactionMode { ReadOnly, ReadWrite }
- pub struct TransactionSpec { pub name: &'static str, pub mode: TransactionMode }
+ #[non_exhaustive]
+ pub struct TransactionSpec { /* private name/mode; constructor and accessors */ }
pub type TransactionFuture<'tx,R> = Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output=Result<R,StorageError>>+Send+'tx>>;
pub trait TransactionProducer<H,R>: Send+Sync+'static {
fn start<'tx>(&'tx self, tx:&'tx mut H)->TransactionFuture<'tx,R>;
}
pub trait StorageRow: Send+Sync+'static {
type Key: Send+Sync+'static;
type New: Send+'static;
fn schema()-> &'static RowSchema;
fn encode(&self)->Result<Vec<Value>,StorageError>;
fn decode(values:Vec<Value>)->Result<Self,StorageError> where Self:Sized;
}
pub trait TransactionHandle: Send {
fn read<T:StorageRow>(&mut self,key:T::Key)->impl Future<Output=Result<Option<T>,StorageError>>+Send;
fn write<T:StorageRow>(&mut self,row:T)->impl Future<Output=Result<(),StorageError>>+Send;
}
// Optional CRUD primitives built for option (a), the proposed template extension,extension; notno domain SQL.
pub trait CrudTransaction: TransactionHandle {
fn insert<T:StorageRow>(&mut self,new:T::New)->impl Future<Output=Result<T,StorageError>>+Send;
fn delete<T:StorageRow>(&mut self,key:T::Key)->impl Future<Output=Result<bool,StorageError>>+Send;
}
pub trait AtomicStorage: Send+Sync {
type Transaction: TransactionHandle;
fn transaction<R:Send+'static,P:TransactionProducer<Self::Transaction,R>>(
&self,spec:TransactionSpec,producer:P
)->impl Future<Output=Result<R,StorageError>>+Send;
}
pub trait Storage<T>: AtomicStorage {
type Key: Send+Sync;
type Error: std::error::Error+Send+Sync+'static;
fn read(&self,key:Self::Key)->impl Future<Output=Result<Option<T>,Self::Error>>+Send;
fn read_all(&self)->impl Future<Output=Result<Vec<T>,Self::Error>>+Send;
fn write(&self,row:T)->impl Future<Output=Result<(),Self::Error>>+Send;
}
```
- StorageError is a typed enum covering encoding/mapping, engine/query, conflict/serialization, suspension, worker failure/panic and closure; no panic/unwrap bridge. RowSchema/Value are backend-neutral table/column/key/value descriptors fixed by the prototype, not SQL strings. Producer owns captures; each retry clones immutable inputs into a fresh future. Result owns its data and cannot leak the transaction handle. Whether transactions span several row types remains an explicit prototype decision, neither promised built nor forbidden. Public APIs always return typed Results.
- SQLite: read-write body is one message to writer, one savepoint in the outer queued-write transaction; all .await must be transaction-handle operations. Call graph is checked by the external analyzer, including transaction-safe-marked callees. A Pending poll is a typed suspension failure with rollback; Ready/Err rolls back, Ready/Ok replies only after outer commit. Read-only may execute on a reader. Writer unwind is caught at the worker boundary; fail every admitted/in-flight/queued reply, close admission and return typed errors to racing submitters. Reader workers use blocking_recv; only writer owns Runtime::block_on per root constraints. PostgreSQL/MySQL default uses real serializable transaction isolation, begin/commit and fresh-body retry on serialization failure. Cancellation rolls back, never commits after refusal.

- Tsql=existing schema::WidgetRow{id:schema::WidgetId,name:String}; Key=schema::WidgetId; draft New={name:String} has no key. Keep api-types CLI DTO identities and existing conversions/errors. WidgetStorage uses the generic atomic unit/CRUD transaction primitives for generated-key insert/delete, pending owner ratification; map typed storage failures to existing StoreCode/StoreError, never strings. Each engine exports generic Store<T> and async open<T:StorageRow>(&EngineConfig)->Result<Store<T>,StorageError>; EngineConfig is table-neutral (SQLite path, Postgres URL, MySQL URL). It validates target and applies the application-supplied row schema before returning. Application-owned OpenWidgetStore translates existing OpenConfig/StoreError, not an engine trait. SQLite Store clones one supplied/shared SqliteDatabase. Generated service Stores implements StoresView and passes its Widgets to common commands. d-5 owns actual schema definitions; d-6/7/8 implement generic Storage<T>/CRUD primitives with arbitrary contract rows; d-10 implements WidgetStorage/OpenWidgetStore application wrappers and consumes them.

Factory/codec definitions live in real writer src/contract.rs and exported lib.rs; contract tests import them. SqliteDatabase::open(path,capacity,readers).await then storage::<T>(mapping).await applies registered generic schema on its writer; no consumer table code in backend. Factory/mapping declarations are frozen before consumers begin. No signature copies remain as an alternate source.
- CronRow wraps existing Schedule without dropping its stored fields. Real awaited CronStorage declarations in sc-cron retain create/get/list_active, fenced record_run/set_next/stop/disable, set_enabled, atomic set_enabled_many/replace_and_set_enabled, limits, query and operation context from STEP3. Implementation in d-9 is CronStore<S:Storage<CronRow>>, using generic transactions for domain read/check/mutate atomically. Table/column mapping and legacy cron.db migration belong to sc-cron, never backend crates. The one shared tests/support/cron-storage crate exports the controlled double plus generic async conformance cases derived from current consumer_contract.rs; d-9 runs double, d-11 runs actual engines. d-5 registers it at boundaries/sc-cron/sc-cron.toml allowed_test_double_paths and as private test support; no second copy of cron types. d-6 uses generic-row conformance only.

- ## External dependencies and prototype acceptance
- No-panic enforcement: randlee/sc-lint#931 (external). Transaction-body await analyzer: second sc-lint rule, external request not yet filed; lead owns that request. Record external state honestly; do not replace either with a grep or a fabricated successful linter. d-5 defines the transaction-safe marker contract with that rule's maintainer, and prototype/runtime tests are separate from static analyzer evidence. Production release requires actual analyzer/no-panic enforcement on changed phase code, or a new explicit user decision; no implicit waiver. Analyzer rejects awaits on non-tx handles and calls to unmarked helpers; runtime non-suspension is an additional check, not proof of static safety.

- ## Staged manifest and source handoffs
- Parallel d-3/d-4/d-5 files do not overlap. d-3 owns command and daemon manifests entirely (including rmcp) through closure. d-10 follows d-3/d-5 and takes command manifest only to register sc-storage. d-5 owns root members/workspace.dependencies registration; d-12 later owns0.3.0 version conversion and Cargo.lock, after consumed owners close. d-5 registers sc-storage/writer/rusqlite baseline in sc-cron/writer/store manifests without deleting old SQLx code. Those files pass to d-9/d-6/d-7/d-8 after d-5 sanity; only those layers remove SQLx SQLite/legacy rusqlite and implement direct SQLx driver imports. Root rusqlite0.41 baseline is shared with retained cron legacy; d-5 absorbs legacy API drift in its explicitly staged sqlite/operation/consumer-contract modules, d-9 later removes them. No backend->sc-cron dependency or optional cron feature remains.

+ StorageError covers mapping/engine/conflict/suspension/worker-failure/closure and provides code(), is_retryable(), source() and recovery(). Writer panic fails every admitted/in-flight/queued reply and closes admission. Read-only workers use blocking_recv without a runtime; only the writer owns Runtime::block_on. The actual transaction-safe analyzer is mandatory; its marker is coordinated with its maintainer, not declared advisory or invented before delivery.

description
## Deliverables
1. Implement genericSQLite's share of the one shared sc-storage Storage<T> trait and namedits single AtomicStorage::transaction(spec, producer) operation for several row operations as one atomic unit; SQLite (d-6), Postgres (d-7) and MySQL (d-8) each implement that same contract (ANC-032/033). The writer thread exclusively owns the only write-mode SQLite connection; reader workers open read-only connections. Futures are NEW work, not copied typed operations. Read-write body is one writer message/savepoint; queue batches commit together and replies follow commit. Read-only may use reader pool — REQ-DBSQ-0002/0003; ANC-022..027/033.

Public storage APIs return typed Result and never panic; writer panic terminates/fails every pending/in-flight/queued caller without hangs — NFR-RUN-0002; ANC-035/036. design
Consumes the real d-5 factory/codec/Storage/transaction declarations and prototype result. Own implementation after explicit staged manifest/lib.rs handoff; no redefinition of contract.rs. OneThe writer thread exclusively owns the only write-mode SQLite connection; one database handle ownsroutes onewrites writerthrough queue/onlyits writequeue, connectionand plusreader workers use read-only workers.connections. Copy only proven channel/reader plumbing from atm-core, implement the new future mechanism with explicit prototype risk. Per root writer constraints, only writer runtime drives Runtime::block_on; readers use blocking_recv, no runtime.
Read-write transaction producer executes in one savepoint inside queued outer transaction; failed/suspended body rolls back that savepoint, outer commit precedes success reply. Owned Send+'static producer creates a fresh future per attempt; SQLite body can await only tx operations. Actual Pending is rejected, even if a call would later become ready. Runtime is not the analyzer. Worker catch_unwind translates panic to typed worker-failed state, drains/fails every outstanding reply and closes admission; subsequent callers get typed failure. No public API panics.
No table-specific code or dependency on sc-cron. Storage<T> uses registered generic descriptor/codec; application chooses/migrates schema through generic engine API. d-6 removes SQLx SQLite only in its owned store wrapper manifest after d-5 additive registration. Package/default features remain consumer-neutral. Direct native identity is proved by cargo tree -i libsqlite3-sys; absence of sqlx-sqlite by cargo tree, not lockfile. description
## Deliverables
-
- 1. Implement the agreed Storage<T> backend using direct sqlx-core/sqlx-postgres Postgres pool/migration code; typed row mapping stays in backend/consumer contract, no raw cross-engine query API — REQ-RUN-0328; PRD-STO2.
- 2. Replace widget-specific store functions only when the typed consumer calls compile; preserve live-engine transaction/error semantics and feature gates — ADR0020; REQ-RUN-0302.
-
- 3. Implement the exact d-5 generic StorageRow/Store<T>/engine factory contract and generated-key create/delete primitives using arbitrary conformance rows and generic atomic transaction begin/commit/retry. App supplies schema mapping; backend has no specific consumer table code — ANC-032/033/034/035.
- 4. Replace sqlx umbrella with direct sqlx-core + engine driver + sqlx-macros requirements, retaining only necessary features; qualify real query macros, migration/offline/CLI paths, not just a successful resolver — REQ-RUN-0002; NFR-RUN-0007.
+ 1. Implement Postgres's share of the one shared sc-storage Storage<T> trait and its single AtomicStorage::transaction(spec, producer) operation for several row operations as one atomic unit; SQLite (d-6), Postgres (d-7) and MySQL (d-8) each implement that same contract (ANC-032/033). Implement PostgresStore<T>: sc-storage Storage<T> plus the same generic AtomicStorage::transaction(spec, producer), generic row mapping, generated-key insert/delete and engine factory. App owns schema/migrations; no WidgetRow, CronRow or consumer SQL lives in the generic engine (ANC-032/033/034/035).
+ 2. Replace the sqlx umbrella with sqlx-core/sqlx-postgres/sqlx-macros >=0.9, no upper bound. Qualify real live query macros, migrations/offline replacement and CLI paths, preserving typed errors and existing wrapper behavior (REQ-RUN-0002/0302/0321; ANC-037).
+ 3. Bound serialization retries and pool-acquire/statement/transaction waits in EngineConfig using finite defaults and validated configuration. Exhaustion/deadline yields typed StorageError with retryability/recovery, never an infinite loop. Controlled conflicts/timeouts test the bound; no sleeps or load races. Phase-d uses engine retry defaults; later transaction-specific retry policy remains possible (NFR-RUN-0002/0009).
## This sprint does not close
Real production composition, generated database security and registry migration are d-11; no generator/sync/permission feature is added.
+ These phase-d transaction-body rules do not prohibit later second transform inputs, typed Ok/no-write outcomes or a transform inside an atomic transaction; those behaviors are not built in this sprint (ANC-051).

boundary:template-store-postgres — contract tests pass against an actual Postgres service with named CI prerequisites, write/read and typed error behavior; workspace/boundary checks pass. A fake/sqlite stand-in is not live Postgres proof. d-11 owns final surfaces/template composition.
## Required validation commands
Generate a development-source consumer with just new <temp-dir> --var-file wizard/fixtures/postgres.json. SQLX_OFFLINE may support query-macro compilation but does not substitute for actual live-engine tests. d-3d-7 owns .github/workflows/store-postgres.yml: provision its real postgres service and POSTGRES_DATABASE_URL, apply migrations, generate the CIconsumer prerequisite/recipewith wiring.the fixture above, then run these same generated-consumer test/clippy/build/boundary commands in its existing normal live job. Preserve REQUIRE_POSTGRES=1 and fail on skipped live tests; no min/latest duplication. Preserve thin legacy wrappers until the replacement consumer compiles; do not create an artificial dependency on the service implementation.

Test minimum/latest direct-crate features and actual live query macros, migrations, offline/sqlx-toml replacement and CLI migration procedures as applicable. A cargo check-only probe is not evidence those paths work.

description
## Deliverables
1. Implement CronStore<S:Storage<CronRow>>CronStore<S:Storage<CronRow> + Storage<MontyBlobRow>> and CronStorage ONCE in sc-cron using the generic atomic unit. Implement only the domain CronStorage surface; keep the underlying Storage<CronRow> backend private and map its typed failures to CronError. Every public storage function implemented or changed here in CronStore/CronStorage, migration and cron-command storage adapters must return a typed Result and must not panic (ANC-035). Own CronRow mapping/schema, active-name/row-limit admission, per-row generation checks, fenced record_run/set_next/stop/disable and atomic set_enabled_many/replace_and_set_enabled — REQ-CRON-0004/0020/0021; ANC-030/031/033/034.
2. Migrate scheduler/worker to awaited app-supplied storage, porting hooks to the single sc-monty interpreter, preserving hooks/Monty,clock-driven clocks,tick dispatch, in-flight skip, cooperative cancellationstop/cancellation and typed FENCED behavior. Existing record_run and set_next still persist execution outcomes and next-run state through the fenced atomic policy operations in deliverable1. Domain read/check/mutate runs in one serializable atomic body, never separate calls. Backend is table-neutral — ADR-RUN-0013/0014/0020.
3. Implement legacy cron.db-to-app-DB migration above generic storage: preserve IDs/generation/run/end/spec/hook state; idempotent import and collision/rollback refusal. Legacy source is read only as explicit migration input, no ongoing second database setting — REQ-CRON-0004.
4. Reuse d-5the sharedported async CronStorage conformance suite owned here against its double; port, never delete, existing assertions. Retire legacy DB files/dependency only after generic suite has equivalent case IDs and double tests pass. Actual engine/two-process provider runs are d-11, not a false double claim. Adapt thin cron-command APIs and READMEsREADMEs. Inspect the resolved normal/build dependency graphs for EACH supported feature set of both published crates, including sc-cron default and monty, and sc-cron-commands default, schema, scheduler, schema+scheduler, monty and schema+monty (monty includes scheduler). Enable the optional scheduler and Monty edges in those inspections; a default-only graph is insufficient. For every inspected feature set: neither may contain any crate from the sc-compose repository except permitted sc-sha, and neither may contain an ATM crate. Dev-only test/benchmark references are outside this production rule; use inspection evidence, with no new checker — REQ-RUN-0702; ANC-012/016/017/019/035.ANC-061/035.
- ## This sprint does not close
- Full real-SQLite/mixed-engine cron conformance is d-11, actual released beads-cache d-12. No storage backend imports sc-cron or specific table code. No separate duplicate cron invariant suite.
+
+ 5. Ask sc-monty to compile the source when a schedule is submitted or updated, rejecting invalid source before any tick. Persist the just-compiled, never-run session blob through Storage<MontyBlobRow> in a sc-cron-owned table. Key it by SHA-256 of the exact source computed with permitted sc-sha, plus the Monty dump version. The schedule source remains authoritative; use a blob only for a matching key. Missing/stale/corrupt/unreadable-version blobs or missing cron_stop/cron_tick are cache misses: recompile from source and overwrite with the pre-run dump. Persist no run/session execution state. Migrate the new cron-owned table through generic row/schema APIs; no storage backend acquires cron SQL/types. — owner item 2.
+ 6. Replace sc-cron's Monty compile/session/limits/host/dump/load implementation with calls to sc-monty. Keep JSON conversion, cron hook names/policy and schedule payload handling here; hooks continue receiving values, never JSON strings. Preserve all copied/ported unit and integration assertions. A schedule accepts Monty or Python script plus JSON data; keep that data available to the app transform before policy-checked persistence. — owner items 1/5, single-implementation and copy rulings.
+
+ ## Boundaries and handoffs
+ Full real-SQLite/mixed-engine cron conformance is d-11, actual released beads-cache d-12. No storage backend imports sc-cron or specific table code. No separate duplicate cron invariant suite. Hand the completed sc-cron-commands files/tests/README/manifest to d-11 for shared-path routing after this sprint sanity; d-11 consumes this policy API and d-10 common helpers in its existing final integration wave.
+ CronStore consumes AtomicStorage::transaction(spec, producer) from the shared Storage<T> contract; d-6/d-7/d-8 implement that same method for SQLite/Postgres/MySQL, while d-9 supplies only cron policy bodies (ANC-033).
+ Retire ScheduleStore/SqliteScheduleStore and legacy SQLite files in0.3.0, updating lib.rs/row.rs/storage.rs after the d-5 handoff. CronStore wraps Storage<CronRow> privately and exposes only policy-checked CronStorage operations. Keep per-name in-flight behavior and generation fencing under local REQ-CRON-0001 and ADR-RUN-0013; upstream crosswalk numbers are provenance, not local requirement IDs.
+ Convert every remaining registry line in crates/sc-cron/Cargo.toml and every registry line in crates/sc-cron-commands/Cargo.toml, including dev/optional entries, to >= tested floors with no upper bound; preserve features. This includes async-trait, chrono, cron, getrandom, tokio, tracing, process-wrap, sc-monty, sc-sha, tempfile and libc; remove direct monty/monty-types dependencies after the shared-interpreter port, plus utoipa >=6.0.0 and schemars >=1.2.3 in sc-cron-commands (ANC-037). The sc-cron Windows declarations inherited from d-5 are win32job >=2.0.3 and waitpid-any >=0.3.0, each with no upper bound; retain those already-open requirements unchanged.
+
+ After the d-5 boundary registration handoff, own boundaries/sc-cron/sc-cron.toml for the actual public-facade/root removals matching this implementation. This is the boundary's own facade, not a shared root registry.
+
+ sc-monty compilation/dump or cache-miss reconstruction is requested before the atomic storage body; interpreter work is not awaited inside that body. Persist the validated schedule/blob through the generic atomic operation while retaining admission/fencing checks (owner item 2; ANC-033).
+
+ Shared-command handoff: cron.start and cron.end use storage_write, cron.list uses storage_read when d-11 integrates d-10 helpers. These are all user-facing cron commands. Consume d-5's passing exact copy of the current Monty code AND unit/integration tests before extending or moving the cron adapter; retain every hook assertion (ANC-062).
+
+ The complete cron command set is: cron.start uses storage_write; cron.end uses storage_write; cron.list uses storage_read. Every cron command uses the shared path. No cron command is excluded (ANC-053/054).
+
+ Every compile, session run, session dump/load and host-function dispatch requested by sc-cron is executed only by sc-monty. sc-cron only selects source/cache entries, converts JSON to Monty values and supplies cron-specific value adapters; it contains no interpreter compiler, session runner or host dispatcher of its own (ANC-041).
+
+ Own sc-cron-commands/Cargo.toml dependency registration for the later library policy adapter, including sc-storage from the d-5 workspace registration at >=0.2.0 during development and >=0.3.0 at release, with no upper bound in either case. Existing sc-command/sc-cron dependencies support d-11 source integration; d-11 adds no dependency or manifest edit. This manifest passes from d-9 directly to d-12 for final release-version lines on their existing dependency path.

+ boundary:sc-cron/row-limit — CronStore refuses to add a schedule row once its row count reaches the embedding application's configured limit; the existing row-limit tests are ported, not deleted (ANC-031).
+ boundary:sc-cron/atomic — set_enabled_many, replace_and_set_enabled and every domain read/check/mutate body call the shared generic transaction operation; several row operations commit or roll back as one atomic unit (ANC-033).

+ boundary:sc-cron/public-storage-functions — The public CronStorage domain operations (create/get/list_active, record_run/set_next/stop/disable, set_enabled/set_enabled_many/replace_and_set_enabled, query/context), migration and storage adapters all return typed Results and do not panic. These are the public storage functions governed by ANC-035, NFR-RUN-0009 and REQ-CRON-0005; exercise their typed-error paths through the shared conformance tests and actual sc-lint#931 rule, with no missing-rule waiver (NFR-RUN-0002).

+ boundary:sc-cron/policy-entry — No raw public CronStore write bypasses active-name, row-limit or fenced-generation policy; the same domain suite exercises all mutation entry points. Mapped StorageError retains typed code/source/recovery alongside stable CronError codes.
+ boundary:sc-cron/compiled-monty — Using the real shared interpreter and controlled storage, submit rejects non-compiling source; successful writes dump immediately after compile, before execution. Restart reloads an unchanged source/version blob without recompiling. Source/version mismatch, missing/corrupt bytes and missing cron_stop/cron_tick each trigger source recompilation and overwrite. The new row/table and migration belong only to sc-cron, with no table-specific backend change. No backend-specific SQL/type/schema enters generic engines; cron mapping and migration remain in sc-cron.

description
## Deliverables
1. Implement the real generated service boundary using sc-storage Storage<Tsql>; implement the two default sc-command storage_read/storage_write combinators once and provide the application read/write path for existing CLI/MCP/HTTP service entrypoints with application-owneddefault plain Tcli/Tsql conversionsconversions, replaceable by application rules and WidgetStore<S> wrapper. — REQ-RUN-0201/0302; PRD-CMD-2/3/4.
2. Add a real Python/Monty-authored transform caller on that path, reusingcalling existingsc-monty hostingdirectly, patternswith withoutruntime-loaded inventingreplaceable asource and no second interpreter host, generator or permissions system. Blocking interpreter/I/O work stays off Tokio request workers. — PRD-CMD-5; NFR-RUN-0002.
3. Document sc-command default helper API/exports in its README, then replace per-layout widget-specific backend calls with the agreed Storage trait and port service behavior/error tests against the contract storage double. — REQ-RUN-0328; ADR0021.
- ## This sprint does not close
+ 4. Route widget.create and widget.delete through storage_write and widget.get through storage_read, preserving WidgetStorage/StoresView domain behavior. A Tcli convertible directly to Tsql uses the default plain conversion without a hand-written transform; custom rules can replace it. — owner items 6/7.
+ 5. Document Transform/storage_read/storage_write as provisional in0.3.0. Use an extensible input/context and typed outcome seam with constructors/defaults so later second input, Ok with nothing written (distinct from Err), and atomic-transaction transforms can be added without breaking consumers. Build none of those three behaviors now and prohibit none. — owner item 4.
+
+ ## Boundaries and handoffs
Real production composition, generated database security and registry migration are d-11; no generator/sync/permission feature is added.
+ After d-3's compiled rmcp3.9 server/schema and public envelope/error compatibility lands, add sc-storage >=0.2.0 (>=0.3.0 at release), with no upper bound, in the handed-off command manifest without changing its already-open registry floors. Define Transform and StorageCommandError beside the plain generic async storage_read/storage_write functions; no StorageCommands wrapper (REQ-CMD-0002; REQ-RUN-0203/0331; ANC-037).
+
+ Transform source comes from an application-owned UTF-8 script file whose path is supplied when configuring the daemon's Monty transform. Read that file at invocation; replacing its contents changes the next invocation without rebuilding. File-read/UTF-8 failures are typed transform errors. Source loading/value conversion are application adapters; all compile/session/host/limits behavior remains solely in sc-monty (ANC-049).
+
+ The complete cron command set is: cron.start uses storage_write; cron.end uses storage_write; cron.list uses storage_read. Every cron command uses the shared path. No cron command is excluded (ANC-053/054).
acceptance_criteria
boundary:template-service — service tests cover real common write/read and Python/Monty transform execution against the contract storage double; typed errors and existing DTO behavior hold; no unfinished branch. Run generated service crate tests/lints and workspace/boundary validation under the configured generation harness. This does not claim production database, transport or release integration; d-11 owns those.
## Required validation commands
Generate a development-source consumer using just new <temp-dir> --var-file wizard/fixtures/postgres.json (no cron selected). Run cargo test --manifest-path <temp-dir>/crates/service/Cargo.toml and cargo clippy --manifest-path <temp-dir>/crates/service/Cargo.toml --all-targets -- -D warnings with required interpreter prerequisites; service contract tests use the controlled storage double and actual Python/Monty transform execution. Then build the generated workspace and run its configured sc-boundary profile. Existing legacy wrappers keep unrelated consumer code compiling until d-11 wiring; no live database or transport proof is claimed here.
Run cargo test -p sc-command --test storage_combinators with the real default combinators and controlled storage/transform errors; no per-app duplicate generic pipeline. No ATM/sc-compose composition-crate or SQLx dependency in the shared storage/command seam.seam; sc-sha is permitted (ANC-061).
boundary:template-service/preserved-crud — Existing create/get/delete/row-delete service behavior, generated IDs and typed errors are unchanged against shared double; default helper implementation/exports and README match the real sc-storage trait. PrototypeImplement the d-5-frozen, owner-ratified option (a) extension remains explicitly pending user ratification,with no silent operation removal.
boundary:template-service/nonblocking — On a controlled single-thread runtime, interpreter worker signals entered then holds on a barrier. While held, an independent async task completes/acknowledges; only that acknowledgment releases the worker. Both success and panic map to typed Results; no sleeps, elapsed deadlines or load races establish correctness. Test cancellation/channel closure deterministically. Storage submission is never wrapped in spawn_blocking. cargo build --workspace passes at closure.
+ boundary:template-service/transform-limits — Before spawn_blocking, acquire a bounded transform permit or return a typed saturation error. Hold that permit until the worker actually exits, including caller cancellation. Apply the published Monty resource/deadline limits to computation itself, map expiry/errors/panic to typed transform errors, and test expiry/saturation/cancellation with controlled inputs. Timing out the JoinHandle alone is not termination proof.
+
+ boundary:shared-command-path — Existing widget.create/delete use storage_write and widget.get uses storage_read. The default command uses direct conversion and Storage<T>, with neither a hand-written transform nor an app-written storage action. Run cargo test -p sc-command --test storage_combinators; cron command routing and its tests are integrated by d-11 after its existing d-9/d-10 prerequisites (ANC-056/059/060/063).
+
+ boundary:runtime-monty-source — Execute a transform through sc-monty, replace its source at run time and invoke again without rebuilding; observe the new result. Exercise the no-cron Postgres generated service; d-11 owns cron-command enrichment integration. The service/sc-command/sc-cron contain no duplicated Monty host. API/README mark the command seam provisional in0.3.0 and explain the three future extensions; no second-input, no-write or atomic-transform behavior is built in phase-d.
+
+ boundary:production-dependencies — The changed normal/build dependency graphs of published sc-command and the generated service contain no ATM crate and no crate from the sc-compose repository except permitted sc-sha; check those existing graph/boundary inputs as well as the seam itself (ANC-061).
+
+ boundary:cron-start-transform — For cron.start the configured application Transform receives the script plus user JSON, may modify/append that JSON, and returns the row input before storage_write invokes the policy adapter/persistence. A registered app transform is always awaited; the direct-conversion default is used only when no custom transform is selected and cannot bypass a selected transform. The test appends an application field and asserts the persisted JSON contains it; a transform error produces no write. d-10 tests the generic helper with its controlled storage double; d-11 exercises the real cron.start adapter and verifies sc-cron passes Monty values, not JSON strings, to the hook (ANC-055/043).

Existing Monty hook internals are reused rather than rewritten as collateral work.

Application service supplies Tcli/Tsql transforms, including real Python/Monty execution, and uses controlled Storage<T> double. No runtime block_on/Handle/futures bridge or sleep in production. Service boundary manifests are generated by d-5 renderer at boundaries/<prefixed-service>/<prefixed-service>.toml; criteria target that emitted boundary/ADR0021.
- Interpreter mechanism: tokio::task::spawn_blocking for synchronous Monty/Python evaluation, following crates/sc-cron/src/monty_run.rs:183 execute_feed_with_logger pattern. It is explicitly allowed for interpreter execution, never to submit/wait for SQLite storage. Transform::apply awaits the JoinHandle and maps interpreter error/panic to typed transform error; no block_on or sleep. Transaction bodies may not call this mechanism or await interpreter/I/O; transformation completes before entering named atomic storage.
- Use schema::WidgetRow/WidgetId, WidgetStorage extension and StoresView exact contracts. Preserve CreateWidget/GetWidget/DeleteWidget/DeleteRow DTO behavior and error codes against the shared double, including store-generated IDs. Common commands come from real sc-storage trait definitions, not cloned contract signatures. Extension design is pending randlee ratification and builds at risk until sign-off.
+ Consumes real d-5 sc-storage Storage/row signatures; implement them once in sc-command/src/storage.rs, exported with the actual implementation. Application service supplies Tcli/Tsql transforms, including real Python/Monty execution, and uses controlled Storage<T> double. No runtime block_on/Handle/futures bridge or sleep in production. Service boundary manifests are generated by d-5 renderer at boundaries/<prefixed-service>/<prefixed-service>.toml; criteria target that emitted boundary/ADR0021.
+ Interpreter mechanism: tokio::task::spawn_blocking for synchronous Monty/Python evaluation, calling sc-monty for all interpreter limits/session/host behavior. It is explicitly allowed for interpreter execution, never to submit/wait for SQLite storage. Transform::apply awaits the JoinHandle and maps interpreter error/panic to typed transform error; no block_on or sleep. Phase-d completes interpreter transformation before entering named atomic storage; in-transaction transforms are not built in this phase. The provisional seam must allow a later atomic transform without breaking consumers.
+ Use schema::WidgetRow/WidgetId, WidgetStorage extension and StoresView exact contracts. Preserve CreateWidget/GetWidget/DeleteWidget/DeleteRow DTO behavior and error codes against the shared double, including store-generated IDs. Common functions consume the real sc-storage Storage<T>/atomic contracts; Transform and command errors are local sc-command types. Consume the option (a) extension frozen and ratified at d-5 closure.
Own the WidgetStore<S> application wrapper over generic Storage<schema::WidgetRow>: map typed errors to existing StoreError, implement WidgetStorage/StoresView and preserve create-with-generated-id/get/delete. The per-layout application factory translates schema::OpenConfig to table-neutral engine config; d-11 injects concrete stores. No table-specific widget code is placed in generic engine crates.
+ Transform execution calls sc-monty directly. Service code contains only application value conversion, runtime source selection and the bounded blocking adapter; no second compile/session/host/limits implementation exists in sc-command, sc-cron or the template. No-cron layouts can select Monty independently, with no sc-cron dependency. Source is loaded at run time and replacing it changes the next invocation without rebuilding. Generic command composition is two free async functions in sc-command; Transform is intentionally open for application implementations.
+
+ Public API shape: storage_write(store, transform, input) and storage_read(store, transform, key) are plain generic async functions over Storage<T>, returning typed StorageCommandError. Built-in read/write behavior and plain conversion cover the default command; no app-written storage action is required. Only cron uses a library-provided policy adapter in sc-cron-commands that delegates to CronStorage; the raw backend stays private and no policy is duplicated. No DefaultStorageCommands type. Transform has compatible default methods and constructor-built, non-exhaustive input/context and outcome types so later second-input/no-write/atomic-transform support does not change these signatures. Only the existing one-input read/write behavior is implemented now.

Use cargo tree -i libsqlite3-sys (one selected>=0.39) and -i sqlx-sqlite (no selected package), never Cargo.lock. Existing CLI/daemon/schema/api-types tests are this sprint's owned regressions. Actual sc-lint#931 no-panic and transaction-body analyzer checks apply to changed template storage code; until delivered and passing, closure remains blocked. Record their actual commands and external state when available; runtime tests never substitute for static analysis.
+ req:REQ-RUN-0328/mixed-dependencies — Direct sqlx-core/engine/macros requirements select NO SQLite feature; cargo tree -i sqlx-sqlite selects no package in sqlite-postgres/sqlite-mysql too. Generated/production crates gain no sc-compose composition-crate or ATM dependency; sc-sha remains permitted, enforced by existing boundary lint (ANC-061/028).
+ req:REQ-CRON-0004/limit — The live shared app database refuses new schedule rows at the embedding app's configured row limit; exercise the ported case against real providers (ANC-031). The conformance suite executes the generic atomic multi-row operation on SQLite, Postgres and MySQL, proving all-or-nothing behavior (ANC-033).
+ req:REQ-RUN-0328/selected-native-tree — The cargo tree of EVERY selected layout (SQLite alone, cron on/off, sqlite-postgres and sqlite-mysql) contains NO sqlx SQLite driver crate. SQLx direct core/driver/macros crates are selected only for Postgres/MySQL; cargo tree -i sqlx-sqlite must select nothing in every case (ANC-028).
+ req:REQ-RUN-0328/generator-compatibility — Generation/setup instructions declare the repository sc-compose CLI minimum as >=1.8.0, using .sc/generation-tools.json as the source. Run the supported layout generation procedures with CLI1.8.0 and compatible CLI commands; generation succeeds at that floor. d-4 owns that declared tool requirement and executable-selection check; d-11 updates the layout instructions and generation tests using it (ANC-003/005).
+ req:REQ-RUN-0328/lifecycle — Using controlled shutdown and writer-failure signals, stop HTTP/MCP intake and scheduler work, drain/cancel in-flight work under the existing grace budget, await SqliteDatabase::shutdown and join its writer before releasing runtime/logger ownership (ADR-RT-0005). Every admitted write commits or returns a typed failure; writer failure stops intake instead of leaving a healthy-looking daemon. Use existing runtime shutdown control, not a new health endpoint.
+
+ req:REQ-RUN-0201/shared-interpreter — Generate Monty with Postgres and cron disabled, build and run its real transform, change source without rebuilding and observe the new value. A cron-selected generated app invokes cron.start/end through storage_write and cron.list through storage_read; these are all cron commands and none bypasses the shared path. The app modifies user JSON before persistence; sc-cron converts it to Monty values, never JSON strings, before passing it to hooks. Widget.create/delete use storage_write and widget.get uses storage_read; the direct-conversion example needs no hand-written transform or app-written storage action. No second Monty host is generated. Existing selected-layout and hook integration assertions remain in force.
+
+ req:REQ-RUN-0201/cron-integration — The actual generated app stores cron rows in its app SQLite file by default, rejects a second active schedule of the same name and a new schedule at the configured row limit through cron.start, and preserves fenced cron.end. Run the ported sc-cron-commands suite and generated CLI/HTTP/MCP integration on the same policy adapter. The generated usage docs state that Transform/storage_read/storage_write are provisional, not yet stable in0.3.0 (ANC-021/030/031/050).
+
+ req:REQ-RUN-0201/cron-submit — cron.start rejects non-compiling source at schedule write, before any tick, through the delivered sc-cron policy API; retain that assertion when routing commands (ANC-048).
+
+ boundary:cron-start-transform — For the implemented Phase D cron.start flow, the configured application Transform receives the script plus user JSON, may modify/append that JSON, and returns the row input before storage_write invokes the policy adapter/persistence. Transform/storage_read/storage_write remain provisional: this current flow does not prohibit later adding a second transform input, a typed Ok outcome with no write distinct from Err, or a transform inside an atomic transaction. Those three behaviors are not implemented in Phase D; the extensible seam delivered by d-10 preserves their later addition. A registered app transform is always awaited; the direct-conversion default is used only when no custom transform is selected and cannot bypass a selected transform. The test appends an application field and asserts the persisted JSON contains it; a transform error produces no write. d-10 tests the generic helper with its controlled storage double; d-11 exercises the real cron.start adapter and verifies sc-cron passes Monty values, not JSON strings, to the hook (ANC-055/043).

description
## Deliverables
1. Migrate actual beads-cache@8e883ee CacheScheduleStore and scheduler calls to published sc-storage/sc-runtime-db-sqlite/sc-cron0.3.0. Deliver the upstream migration PR and validate app+cron writes through its shared writer, preserving existing data and cron behavior — REQ-RUN-0002; REQ-CRON-0004; ADR-RUN-0020.
2. Own registry runner/workflow, archive rehearsal and actual eight-cratenine-crate coordinated0.3.0 publication in dependency order with sc-storage first. Run fresh registry-only upstream/cron, server/rmcp and test-util helper consumers atwith minimum/latestthe allowedrelease-tested ranges,dependency combination, with advisory/source/native-identity checks — REQ-RUN-0002/0702; NFR-RUN-0007; ANC-012/016/017/019.ANC-061.
3. Update root README, release notes/project status and applicable controlled-host benchmark evidence to the actual published surface. Preserve kit/recovery rules and do not claim a source checkout or copied facade is the upstream migration — REQ-RUN-0702; NFR-RT-0001.
- ## This sprint does not close
- Generated app composition/transports are d-11, an independent sibling. No duplicate template wiring or template-only registry subject. Phase release acceptance requires d-11 independently; this sprint does not wait for or repeat its wiring artifact.
+ 4. Remove tests/integration/cron-consumer/schema/Cargo.toml rmcp =3.8.0 pin in this sole-owned consumer manifest: use >=3.9 because3.9.x is the tested patched minimum for RUSTSEC-2026-0462 under the ADR-RUN-0203 amendment. Raising the floor removes older vulnerable releases; every later release from3.9 is admitted with no upper bound. Preserve the existing server/default-features selection and run the normal registry consumer tests and apply req:REQ-RUN-0002/package-caps (ADR-RUN-0203; ANC-037). Also convert tests/integration/cron-consumer/Cargo.toml Windows dev-dependencies to win32job >=2.0.3 and waitpid-any >=0.3.0, preserving purpose comments and running the normal Windows tests. d-3/d-5/d-9 retain their own pin-line edits; this sprint does not repeat them.
+
+ 5. Reuse d-3's check_dependency_manifests(paths) on exact unpacked archives and generated-template defaults; wire it into archive rehearsal, registry consumer validation and upload. Own only input assembly and release fixtures. Published SDK and template registry requirements use >= tested floors with no upper bound. Only consumers may choose pins in their own application manifests or lockfiles; that permission never applies to SDK or template dependency declarations (ANC-037). Remove the interim rule after equivalent sc-lint#936 release and adoption, as recorded by ADR-RUN-0005.
+
+ 6. Own final recommendation generation after0.3.0 conversion and registry availability: template/scripts/tested_dependencies.py, template/cargo-generate.toml and template/.sc-runtime/** deliver the newest tested Cargo.lock and matching .sc-runtime/tested-dependencies.json for each supported profile (ANC-038). The script runs after normal project-name prefixing. Verify every recorded name/version/source matches the lock and real --locked build/tests; consumer pins remain free. Wire this generation into the standing release process through the owned release/publish-preflight.toml and release configuration: every release regenerates and includes its tested Cargo.lock and .sc-runtime/tested-dependencies.json in the delivered template, and generation carries both into populated repositories (ANC-038).
+
+ ## Boundaries and handoffs
+ Generated app composition/transports are d-11-owned. This sprint prepares alongside d-11, consumes d-3's checker, and merges completed d-11 before archive rehearsal/upload. No duplicate template wiring, template-only registry subject or second checker.
+ Apply template/cargo-generate.toml changes only after the completed d-11 merge: preserve its existing layout/cron choices and validation hook, remove Cargo.lock suppression as needed for recommendation delivery and add the recommendation script after project-name prefixing. No concurrent section ownership.
+
+ Include sc-monty as the ninth coordinated0.3.0 public crate in exact archive rehearsal, publication, registry-only consumers and per-release recommendation metadata. Its actual dependency graph permits first-wave publication independently of sc-storage; sc-cron and Monty-enabled services consume that published crate. No template/scheduler/command copy of its interpreter is shipped (owner item 1).
+
+ In the actual migrated consumer, the complete user cron command set is cron.start/end via storage_write and cron.list via storage_read, using the delivered policy adapter. Preserve the application's ability to append/modify user JSON before schedule persistence; the existing consumer tests exercise this path against published crates (ANC-053/054/055).
+
+ The consumer migration retains the provisional command contract: phase-d builds no second-input, typed no-write or in-transaction transform behavior, and its transaction-body rules do not prohibit adding those behaviors later (ANC-051).
+
+ The complete cron command set is: cron.start uses storage_write; cron.end uses storage_write; cron.list uses storage_read. Every cron command uses the shared path. No cron command is excluded (ANC-053/054).

design
## Exact released-consumer subject
beads-cache source8e883ee99cb9c34dfb89fb39e25323d54ae6f2ad uses path sc-cron and already stores schedules in its app DB through CacheScheduleStore (`crates/bd-cache-store/src/schedule.rs:80,164`). Record the source and intentional API changes in tests/registry/phase-d/beads-cache/README.md. Migrate that adapter and actual scheduler calls to sc-cron CronStore over Storage<CronRow> backed by the published generic sc-runtime-db-sqlite shared channel writer. Retain existing application/schedule rows, stable identifiers, generation fencing, row limits and atomic multi-row transitions. No local path/patch/Git SDK dependency can satisfy final acceptance. A recorded source reduction is not falsely described as an upstream beads-cache PR having landed; if the actual migration needs an upstream PR, coordinate it with its owner and retain the outcome as a release predicate.
The manifestrelease-test lock selects the adopted exact release identities for sc-storage, sc-runtime-db-sqlite, sc-cron and applicable runtime/command packages from crates.io. The exact selection is a release-test identity, not a restrictive production third-party range. Direct rusqlite uses the qualifiedowner-directed compatible>=0.41 enveloperequirement with no upper bound and required bundled/hooks/functions/trace features.features; d-12 releases that d-6-qualified uncapped range, without a capped qualification fallback. Verify one libsqlite3-sys>=0.39; validaterun actualnormal rangestests atwith minimum/latest.the selected versions. No SQLx SQLite driver remains in the generated SQLite consumer. SQLx PostgreSQL/MySQL-only graphs must not gain a SQLite native edge; a selected SQLite feature would change that exposure and is not inferred absent from a crate name.
## Registry runner/workflow interface
Own `.github/workflows/phase-d-registry.yml` and `tests/registry/phase-d/run.py` together. The workflow invokes `python3 tests/registry/phase-d/run.py --endpoint minimum|latest --version <adopted-version> --source crates-io`; the version has one adopted source. It checks the migrated beads-cache subject, server/rmcp and test-util helper subjects, plus the actual migrated beads-cache SQLite+cron application. Later user decisions reflected in final itemsThe final items reflect the later user decisions. There is one app DB, and cron is CronStore over Storage<CronRow> (d-9, d-11).
